Rohit Verma: Weird edge-case in the Python SDK quickstart: after a 502 we got two resources created even though the client retried only once. Repro below.
Zoe Kim: Logs? Is this a missing Idempotency-Key or something else?
Rohit Verma: Logs snippet: ```
2024-12-01T11:03:05Z WARN req=a1 status=502 upstream_error
2024-12-01T11:03:05Z INFO retrying req=a1 attempt=2 backoff=0.8s
2024-12-01T11:03:06Z INFO request=req=b2 status=201 created=task-42
```
Lily Wong: Quickstart uses streaming multipart upload for attachments, right? Async generator body is single-use, so retry behavior is different.
Rohit Verma: Exactly. The first try probably sent body then timed out at gateway; the retry sent a truncated/malformed body and backend processed it as a new create. No Idempotency-Key was provided in the example.
Zoe Kim: Two fixes: (1) quickstart should show `idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4())` for write ops, (2) SDK should surface an opt-in `stream_replay` for async helpers to buffer small uploads for retries.
Lily Wong: Also noticed auth middleware refresh can rebuild headers and accidentally drop per-request headers during refresh. If Idempotency-Key was present originally it can be lost on retry.
Rohit Verma: Repro snippet I used: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os, uuid
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('API_KEY'))
client.create_job({'title':'demo'}, idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()), timeout=2)
```
Zoe Kim: Good. Short-term: update quickstart to pass idempotency_key in the sample and mention 502/504 and client-side timeouts as uncertain. Medium-term: add `auto_idempotency` for the helper (opt-in) and a typed param `stream_replay: Literal['never','buffer_mem','spool_disk']='never'` for async parity.
Lily Wong: Tests: add unit that mocks 502 then 201 and assert a single server-side create when idempotency present and buffer enabled. Also test that auth refresh preserves request headers (case-insensitive merge).
